newsitem.title: USA: Fannie Mae sees housing market slowing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae sees housing market slowing in 1997.

text.p: Home sales will moderate in 1997 due to a slower economy and weaker job market, even if mortgage rates decline, David Berson, chief economist for Federal National Mortgage Association, said on Thursday.

The slower housing market, combined with fewer refinancings, will result in a 10 percent drop to $710 billion in mortgage originations next year, Berson said delivering Fannie Mae's annual economic outlook.
Berson said that amount would still make 1997 the fifth best year ever and compared to 1996's $785 billion, the third highest level ever.
Fannie Mae expects the U.S. economy to slow in 1997, growing by about two percent. "The risks of even slower growth in 1997 have risen, but the best bet remains slow-to-moderate growth," Berson said.
Berson said Fannie Mae does not expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next year.

"The chances are not zero, however, and as long as unemployment stays low and wage rates are edging upward, there is a risk of Fed tightening," Berson said. "At this point, however, no change in policy is the most likely course."
